[P1] 西游记之卅四
天竺国
天竺国
《西游记》之三十四
原著 吴承恩
改编 陈平夫
绘画 彭国昌
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
这本画册是根据古典文学名著《西游记》第九十三回一九
十五回改编的。描述的是唐僧师徒四人，路过天竺国和蜈蚣
岭时除掉玉兔妖和蜈蚣精的故事。情节生动有趣，表现了孙
悟空见义勇为，为民除害的高尚品质。

1  唐僧师徒四人往西天取经，一路上跋山涉水，降妖
除怪，走了十四年之久，眼看接近西天。一日傍晚，师徒
正要投宿，路旁闪出一座大庙，山门上写着斗大金字:“布
金禅寺”。

[P3] 2 唐僧在马上沉思道：‘布金……莫不是到了‘舍卫国’界了么？’八戒忙问：‘师父，你认识路呀？’唐僧道：‘佛经里面说，有个给孤独长者，请佛讲经，用金砖布地，想是这个典故。’
3 八戒道：‘走运！但愿是这个地方，我们也抢块金砖送人！’悟空‘啐’了八戒一口，忙扶唐僧下马，大家笑着进了山门。

[P4] 4 山门下，挤满了挑担的、推车的、背包的、牵牲口的客商，横躺竖卧，有说有笑。一见八戒、沙僧、悟空过来了，马上鸦雀无声，你躲我闪，让出一条路来。
5 师徒四人转过金刚殿，迎面出来一位老和尚，唐僧连忙上前施礼，自报来历，老和尚听了说：‘原来是大唐神僧到了，请到室内用茶！’

[P5] 6 寺里大小和尚，都来参见唐僧。唐僧问起‘布金寺’来由，老和尚一讲，正是佛经上那个典故。八戒听了，满地乱瞅金砖，引得悟空、沙僧暗里发笑。
7 唐僧问山门下为啥有那么多客商？众和尚说：‘这‘百脚山’下，有座鸡鸣关，近年来常有蜈蚣精拦路伤人。这班行商，在庙里借宿，等候五更鸡叫时，蜈蚣躲开，才好过关赶路。’

[P6] 8 唐僧对悟空说：‘我们也要鸡叫时动身。’八戒马上张大了嘴打个呵欠，向老和尚说：‘快找地方睡觉，鸡叫就走！’老和尚说：‘是的，住处早给师父们安置好了。’
9 月明如昼。唐僧同悟空正在廊下散步，只见来个小和尚说：‘神僧爷爷，院主看你们来了！’跟着走来一位老和尚。一路行礼道：‘中华来的师父，失迎！失迎！’唐僧连忙答礼相迎。

[P7] 10 院主对唐僧师徒取经，能来到这里，十分敬仰。谈得不愿离去了，说：‘冬夜月光皎洁，该到“给孤独长者”请佛讲经旧址去看看。不过，风去楼空，早成一片荒凉空地。’
11 唐僧和悟空欣然愿往，院主叫小和尚开了后门，四人边走边谈，觉得累了，就坐在土台上歇息。这时，一碧晴空，夜深人静，忽听有人啼哭，娇滴滴的，是个女孩子声音。

[P8] 12 唐僧感触心酸，不觉泪下。问道：‘什么人哭呀？’院主见问，连忙打发小和尚走开，对着唐僧跪倒便拜。唐僧搀起院主道：‘老院主，为何行此大礼？有话慢慢讲来。’
13 原来去年今晚，院主正在念经，忽听风过后传来一阵哭声，急忙寻找，在后门外见一女子，问道：‘你是谁家女子？为何到此啼哭？’那女子道：‘我是天竺国公主，在月下观花，被风刮来的。’

[P9] 14 院主一时难辨真假，又怕一个少女住在庙里出了乱子，便把她砌在一间空房里，只留一个能递饭碗的小洞。众和尚围拢来看，院主说：‘是个妖邪，被我捉住锁起来了。’
15 那女子听了，马上解透了院主的意思，便装疯作傻，白天胡言乱语，夜深人静时，才敢偷着哭爹叫娘。日子久了，庙里和尚，谁也不再来理她了。

[P10] 16 院主几次进城打听，都没消息，国王住的深宫禁地，也不能去问。只得每天送些粗茶淡饭养她活命，转眼之间，已经一年了。
17 院主谈到这里，又拜了几拜说：‘看她美貌端庄，像是公主。其中情由，万望老师父见了国王辨明，若能救拔善良，不仅这女子感你恩德，就连小僧我能了却这桩心事，也忘不了您的好处。’唐僧慨然答应。

[P11] 18 唐僧心事重重，难以入睡，不觉金鸡报晓，山门下人唤马叫。唐僧也唤醒众徒，收拾行囊，准备动身。这时，进来个和尚说：‘老院主请师父们吃点心哩。’
19 八戒见吃就乐，一盘馍馍下肚，眉开眼笑，牵马先行。唐僧辞谢众僧，师徒四人离了布金寺，跟那伙行商，哄哄嚷嚷，一同上了大路。

[P12] 20 晨色朦胧，“鸡鸣关”上，寒风袭人，远近鸡叫声，
不绝于耳。
21 黎明时分过了关，早饭后进入天竺国皇城。众商人
各寻旅店。唐僧师徒便投“会同馆驿”住下。

[P13] 22 驿丞（馆驿的头儿）问明了唐僧的来历去向，招待更加殷勤。唐僧提到去见国王，驿丞说：‘正好！今天是公主抛彩招婿之期，国王满心欢喜，保你一去就能换照放行。’
23 八戒一听公主招婿，心里痒痒地说：‘今天我保师父上朝。’沙僧说：‘二哥，你的嘴脸太丑，还是让大哥去吧。’唐僧点头同意。八戒把嘴一撇说：‘哼！叫我看咱三个的嘴脸都不好看！’

[P14] 24 唐僧换上袈裟，悟空背起文袋，出了馆驿门，只见街满巷塞，熙熙攘攘，都是去彩楼看抛绣球招驸马的人。
25 悟空要跟着去看，唐僧不准。悟空说：‘师父，到彩楼，一定能看到公主，不正好辨辨真假么。’唐僧连连点头说：‘对，我一时疏忽，把院主嘱托的事倒给忘了，走吧。’

[P15] 26 师徒二人，卷入人群，身不由主，推推拥拥挤到彩楼前面去了。
27 原来这公主是个妖精变的。它知道唐僧路经天竺国，便把真公主摄走；又假借抛彩招婿，要破坏唐僧取经。正当中午，那妖精装作千娇百媚，由几十个宫女服侍，上了彩楼。

[P16] 28 妖精一眼望见唐僧，取过绣球便抛，不偏不斜正落在唐僧头上。唐僧大吃一惊，心想用手扫开，说也真怪，那绣球反而滚到袖筒里去了。
29 楼上齐喊：‘打着和尚了！’楼下大乱，那些专来接彩的公子哥儿，还有想撞撞运气的富商子弟，一拥而上，围住唐僧，要抢彩球。

[P17] 30 悟空大怒，高喝一声，一躬腰长了三丈多高，吓得那班公子哥儿和富家子弟们，喊爹叫娘，跌跌爬爬，全逃跑了。
31 悟空还了原象。只见宫娥、太监下楼，来对唐僧下拜道：“贵人，请入朝堂贺喜吧。”唐僧连忙搀起众人，回头埋怨悟空道：“你这猴头，又来捉弄我!”

[P18] 32 悟空笑道：‘是您同意来的，彩球打在你头上，干我什么事呢。’唐僧转怒为愁道：‘你看怎么办哪？’悟空和唐僧耳语了一阵，最后说：‘这叫‘依婚降妖计’，记住！我回馆驿去了。’
33 唐僧被宫娥拥到楼前，只得同公主登辇入朝，去见国王。

[P19] 34 国王一见驸马是个和尚，心中不喜。唐僧忙把来历讲了，最后恳切地说：‘万望国王念我是个和尚，不能与公主成婚。恕我死罪，倒换关文，打发我早赴西天，小僧感恩不尽！’
35 国王有意放走唐僧，怎奈公主死不肯依。国王马上换了笑颜对公主说：‘这也是‘千里姻缘一线牵’啊，既然公主欢喜，待孤传旨晓喻天下，选择吉日，与儿成婚好了。’

[P20] 36 唐僧并不谢恩，一个劲儿地叫：“放我取经去吧！”国王把脸一沉说：“好个不通情理的和尚，朕以一国之富，招你做个驸马，为何不知享受？再提‘取经’二字，推出斩首！
37 唐僧胆战心惊，想起悟空的妙计，连忙奏道：“贫僧谢恩！不过，我想嘱咐我三个徒弟几句话，打发他们去取经行么？”国王准奏，对内侍道：“快到馆驿传那三个小和尚来见。”

[P21] 38 再说悟空从彩楼回去，对八戒、沙僧一讲，八戒捶胸顿脚道：‘这美事儿，师父又是不干，要叫我去多好，绣球只要落在我老猪头上，我可不用推推拥拥，便跑去拜天地了。’
39 沙僧指着八戒的鼻子羞辱了一顿，八戒不依，两个人正吵闹间，只见驿丞来报道：‘圣上有旨，传三位小师父上殿哩。’

[P22] 40 八戒道：‘师父做了驸马，来请我们吃喜酒哩！’悟空心里明白，把脸一沉说：‘不要乱讲，快收拾收拾，上朝见师父去吧。’
41 悟空三人上了金殿，昂立不跪。悟空一看师父在殿旁侍立，怒喝道：‘国王大理不通！我师父既是贵人，怎么连个座位也没有呀！’

[P23] 42 国王见他们相貌丑陋，不由大惊失色，真想溜走，又怕失了体统，连忙叫人取绣墩来，请唐僧坐下。又硬着胆子问道：‘三位圣僧快把来历报来？’
43 三人一讲来历，一个是‘齐天大圣’，一个是‘天篷元帅’，一个是‘卷帘将军’，慌得国王下了龙床，走近唐僧恭恭敬敬地说：‘驸马，小女得配活佛，幸甚！幸甚！’

[P24] 44 国王正在欢喜，忽有阴阳官奏道：“下官奉旨查看历书，明天就是吉日……” 国王听了高兴地说：“快把御花园打扫干净，请驸马同三位高徒安歇。并安排嫁妆、筵席，明日成婚。”
45 国王退朝，文武散班。唐僧一到御花园住处，便扯过悟空道：“你这猢狲，害我好苦，眼看明天就要成婚，叫我怎么办哪？”

[P25] 46 悟空道：‘师父别急，前天在彩楼前，因为没看见公主模样，所以难辨真假。明天拜堂，我一看便知，要是妖精，我便拿她；要是公主，你就做个驸马爷，在这里享享荣华多好啊。’
47 唐僧一听更恼，骂道：‘你再胡说，我可念咒啦！’悟空忙说：‘别念！别念！我是说笑话哩。若是真公主，等拜堂时，我们大闹皇宫，还怕不能把你领走吗？’

[P26] 48 唐僧这才放心。八戒道：‘放着驸马爷不做，要当和尚。算了，算了，素斋摆上多时，你们不去吃，我可要去吃饱睡觉了。’
49 再说宫里筹备婚礼，忙成一团，灯火辉煌，如同白昼。国王心喜，正要到御花园去看看驸马，忽有内宫官奏道：‘万岁，正宫娘娘有请！’

[P27] 50 国王进宫，三宫皇后都来朝拜。国王拉过公主问道：
“你抛彩招婿，得配圣僧，想已心满意足了吧？”正宫娘娘接道：“快把你的心事，对父王说吧。”
51 公主跪下奏道：“小女听说驸马有三个徒弟，长得十分丑恶，小女怕见他们……。”国王道：“孩儿不提，我几乎忘了，是不能让他们参加婚礼，明天一早一定打发他们出城。”

[P28] 52 第二天一早，国王差官来请唐僧，悟空想：‘这时来请，一定是打发我们走，好留师父成婚……’便对唐僧说：‘国王若打发我们先走，你只管应承，我闪身就来保护你，别怕。’
53 师徒见了国王。国王请悟空近前道：‘这是加过印的关文，给你。另有金银三十锭作盘缠，送你们早到西天，取经回来，还有重赏。留驸马在此，你们不必挂念。’

[P29] 54 悟空不收金银，拿过关文，转身就走。慌得唐僧一把扯住，咬牙切齿恨道：‘你们都不顾我就走了？’
55 悟空捏着唐僧的手掌，丢个眼色道：‘你在这里做驸马，我们取了经，回来看你。’那唐僧似信非信，还是不肯放手。

[P30] 56 国王连忙请唐僧上殿，并命官员送悟空等即刻动身，唐僧只得撒手。三人走下金殿时，八戒不住地回头张望，问悟空道：“我们当真要走呀？”
57 悟空不言不语，引八戒、沙僧先回馆驿，对他俩说：“你二人在这里别动，谁问什么，就推不知道，待我去保护师父。”

[P31] 58 好大圣，拔根毫毛，吹口气叫：“变！”马上变了个假相留在馆驿，真身早跳到空中去了。
59 悟空又一个翻身，变了个小蜜蜂，嗡的一声，飞回金殿，落在唐僧的帽沿上，悄悄地叫道：“师父，我来了。”

[P32] 60 唐僧听了，才觉心宽。不大一会儿，宫官来请会亲，国王大喜，对唐僧说：‘贵人，时辰已到，该到鸳鸯宫赴合卺筵去了。’
61 唐僧随国王到了后宫，只见悬灯结彩，鼓乐喧天。宫娥彩女，如花似锦。唐僧愁锁眉间，连看也不看一眼。

[P33] 62 少时，皇后、嫔妃簇拥着公主出来了，悟空一看便说：‘师父，公主是个假的，待我使出法身拿它！’唐僧忙说：‘不可！不可！别惊吓了国王。’
63 悟空哪里容得，大喝一声，现了本相，一把揪住公主骂道：‘大胆孽畜！你在这里弄假成真，害得国王骨肉分离，还敢骗我师父，今天就是你的末日到了！’

[P34] 64 鸠鹊宫中齐哭乱叫，乱成一团。唐僧慌了手脚，战兢兢地抱住国王道：‘别怕，别怕，这是我顽徒在施展法力。’
65 那妖精见瞒不过，挣脱了手，丢下穿戴，跑到御花园土地庙里，取出一条碓嘴样的短棍，回头乱打悟空，悟空使棒相迎，棍来棒往，打得难解难分。

[P35] 66 打着打着，各显神通，腾云驾雾，杀在半空。吓得满朝文武胆战，全城百姓心惊，国王捂住眼直打哆嗦。唐僧说：‘国王别怕，你公主是个妖邪，等拿住它你一看就明白了。’
67 有些胆大的妃子，把那衣服钗环拿来给娘娘看了说：‘这是公主穿的戴的，如今赤身露体与那和尚争打，必定是个妖邪。’这时，国王、后妃，定了定神，才敢看了一眼。

[P36] 68 两个人斗了半天，不分胜败。悟空把棒丢起，叫声：
“变！”马上一变十，十变百，百变千，……半空中好似蛇
翻蟒滚、乱打妖邪。
69 妖邪慌了手脚，化道清风逃走，悟空收棒紧追，看
看赶到西天门，悟空叫道：“把天门的，快挡住妖邪，别放
它走了！”

[P37] 70 妖邪一转头，直奔正南，悟空尾追不放。忽至一座大山，一眨眼工夫，妖邪不见了。
71 悟空寻不到妖邪，又怕它遁身回宫，暗害师父，便认准这山的样子，一个跟头，回转天竺国去了。

[P38] 72 悟空降落宫中，见了师父一讲，国王听了，拉住唐僧道：‘既然公主是个妖邪，我那真公主哪里去了？’悟空应道：‘待我拿住假的，真的自然就回来了。’
73 这时，国王、后妃不再惧怕，上前围住悟空下拜道：‘求圣僧快救公主回宫吧！’悟空道：‘国王与我师父上殿，娘娘们回宫，召我师弟来保护师父，我好去降妖。’

[P39] 74 国王连说：‘遵命！’悟空见八戒、沙僧到来，嘱咐一番，一个跟斗云，腾空而去。满朝文武看了，一个个望空叩拜。
75 悟空又回到那座山上寻找，还是不见踪影。唤来土地问道：‘这山何名？有多少妖邪？快讲，饶你罪过！’土地道：‘这山叫毛颖山，山里只有几处兔穴，向来不藏妖邪。’

[P40] 76 悟空把刚才追妖之事一讲，土地大吃一惊，忙说：
“唉呀！小神倒不知道，那……小神快引大圣去找吧！
77 土地引悟空满山寻找，惊动野兔四处乱窜。寻到山顶，见一大窟，用石块堵住窟门，土地道：‘这里象有妖邪，
大圣进去捉吧。’

[P41] 78 悟空用棒捣碎石块，那妖邪猛地冲了出来，且战且走，恶狠狠地揪住土地骂道：‘谁叫你引他来找的呀，死老头子，回头再找你算账！’
79 妖邪在前面跑，悟空在后面追。眼看妖邪支持不住，悟空举棒要打，忽听空中有人叫道：‘大圣，莫动手！棒下留情！’

[P42] 80 喊话的，原来是太阴星君和嫦娥仙子。悟空听他们一讲，才知这妖是广寒宫的玉兔，私自打开金锁，出宫作怪。悟空一想道：‘怪不得它使的武器我不认识，原来是捣药杵呀！’
81 悟空又一想，它冒充公主，招骗师父，忍不住就是一棒。多亏星君拦挡，那妖闪躲得快，棒头未碰着要害，没被打死。

[P43] 82 星君一再求情，悟空道：“饶倒可饶，不过，你得叫它现了原形，拿到天竺国叫国王看看。”星君点头答应。回头用手一指，那妖就地一滚，马上变成了一只玉兔。
83 星月皎洁，国王与唐僧正盼着悟空捉妖回来，忽听空中叫道：“国王，皇后，嫔妃，百官都来观看，这二位是太阴星君和嫦娥仙子，这个玉兔儿，就是你家的假公主……”

[P44] 84 国王等看了，一个个望空叩拜。只见金光一闪，悟空降落殿前，星君、嫦娥、玉兔早已不见了。
85 国王请悟空上殿问道：‘多谢神僧捉了假公主，可真公主在哪里呢？’悟空笑道：‘假的不去，真的不来，现已深夜，天明我还你个真公主就是了。’

[P45] 86 一夜无话。天一亮，国王就请来唐僧师徒寻问公主之事。唐僧把‘布金寺’所见所闻讲了一遍，国王放声大哭，马上传旨，亲到‘布金寺’去接公主。
87 国王约唐僧师徒同行。悟空把腰一扭，早到寺中。找到院主一讲，惊动全寺和尚，一个个换上袈裟，摆好香案，准备迎接国王。

[P46] 88 悟空在寺里等了半天，国王才到。国王恨不得立刻见到公主，就命院主引路前往。公主一见人来，又在装疯胡说，院主跪奏道：‘这位装疯的女子，就是去年风刮来的公主。’
89 国王命快开门，皇后认出公主面容，不顾肮脏，抱头大哭，骨肉至情，引得众人无不下泪。

[P47] 90 公主沐浴更衣。国王命公主先谢唐僧师徒救命之恩，再谢院主供养之情。封院主为‘报国僧官’，传旨重修寺院，众僧谢恩毕，国王摆驾还朝。
91 回国后，唐僧告辞西行，国王苦留不住，于是摆宴饯行，吩咐画像供奉，又封厚礼相谢，唐僧婉词谢绝。悟空道：“只要国王答应一事，比画像、厚礼，都强多了。”国王忙说：“请吩咐吧！”

[P48] 92 悟空道：‘布金寺’前有座‘百脚山’，山中蜈蚣拦路伤人，国王可选壮大雄鸡千只，撒放山中，除此毒害，便利商旅，岂不是一件大大的好事么？
93 国王大喜，马上选来红冠大公鸡千只，送到‘百脚山’中。说也真怪，几丈长的蜈蚣精，一见鸡群，便成直棍一条，任其啄食。只一天工夫，‘百脚山’中的大小蜈蚣都被公鸡吃光了。

[P49] 94 ‘百脚山’改名‘宝华山’，从此日夜通行。唐僧师徒的画像，供在山顶“神僧阁”上，天竺国的君臣百姓，永远纪念着这四位取经的和尚。欲知后事，请看最后一册《灵山参佛祖》。

Tianzhu Kingdom
Tianzhu Kingdom
Journey to the West, Chapter 34
Original work: Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by: Chen Pingfu
Illustrated by: Peng Guochang
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
This picture book is adapted from the classical literary masterpiece "Journey to the West," specifically from chapters 93 to 95. It describes the story of the four disciples of Tang Sanzang as they pass through Tianzhu Kingdom and Wugong Ridge, defeating the Jade Rabbit demon and the centipede spirit. The plot is lively and interesting, showcasing Sun Wukong's noble qualities of bravery and helping the people.

1  The four disciples of Tang Sanzang are traveling west to obtain scriptures. Along the way, they cross mountains and rivers, subduing demons and monsters, having traveled for fourteen years and now nearing the Western Heaven. One evening, as they were about to find lodging, a large temple suddenly appeared by the roadside, with huge golden characters on its gate: "Bujin Chan Temple."

[P3] 2 Tang Sanzang thought to himself while on horseback: 'Bujin... Could this be the border of the 'Shewei Kingdom'? Pig Eighty hurriedly asked: 'Master, do you know the way?' Tang Sanzang replied: 'The Buddhist scriptures mention a wealthy man named Giduolu who invited the Buddha to preach, and covered the ground with gold bricks. This must be that story.'
3 Pig Eighty said: 'Lucky! If this is the place, let's grab a gold brick to give away!' Wukong spat at Pig Eighty, quickly helped Tang Sanzang dismount, and everyone laughed as they entered the temple gate.

[P4] 4 At the mountain gate, the area was crowded with merchants carrying loads, pushing carts, carrying bags, and leading livestock, lying and sitting in all directions, chatting and laughing. As soon as they saw Zhu Bajie, Sha Wujing, and Sun Wukong approaching, they instantly fell silent, scrambling out of the way to make a path.
5 The four disciples turned past the Vajra Hall, where an old monk came forward to greet them. Tang Sanzang hurriedly bowed and introduced himself. Upon hearing this, the old monk said: 'Ah, it's the great monk from the Tang Dynasty! Please come inside for some tea!'

[P5] 6 The monks of all ranks in the temple came to pay respects to Tang Sanzang. Tang asked about the origin of 'Bu Jin Temple'. After the old monk explained, it turned out to be the very story from the Buddhist scriptures. Upon hearing this, Bajie looked around the floor for gold bricks, which made Wukong and Sha僧 laugh secretly.
7 Tang Sanzang asked why there were so many merchants at the temple gate. The monks replied: 'Below this 'Baijiao Mountain', there is a Ji Ming Pass. In recent years, a centipede demon has often blocked the road and harmed people. These merchants stay at the temple overnight, waiting for the rooster to crow at the fifth watch, when the centipede hides, so they can safely pass through the pass and continue their journey.'

[P6] 8 Tang Sanzang said to Wukong: 'We will also set out when the rooster crows.' Bajie immediately opened his mouth wide, yawned, and said to the old monk: 'Quick, find a place to sleep, we'll leave when the rooster crows!' The old monk replied: 'Yes, accommodations have already been arranged for you masters.'
9 The moon was bright as day. Tang Sanzang and Wukong were strolling under the veranda when a little monk came and said: 'Master monk, the abbot has seen you coming!' Then an old monk followed, bowing as he walked: 'Master from China, we apologize for the delay! We apologize for the delay!' Tang Sanzang hurriedly returned the greeting.

[P7] 10 The abbot, deeply admiring Tang Sanzang and his disciples for their journey to fetch scriptures, was reluctant to part with them. He said, 'The winter night is bright with moonlight. We should go to see the old site where the 'Gedulun Elder' invited the Buddha to preach. However, the wind has blown away the buildings, and it has long become a desolate wasteland.'
11 Tang Sanzang and Wukong gladly agreed to go. The abbot had a young monk open the back gate. The four walked and talked, and when they felt tired, they sat on a earthen platform to rest. At that moment, the sky was clear and blue, the night deep and quiet, when suddenly they heard someone crying, a soft, girlish voice.

[P8] 12 Tang Sanzang felt deeply moved and tears welled up in his eyes. He asked, 'Who is crying?' Upon hearing the question, the abbot hurriedly sent the young monk away and knelt before Tang Sanzang. Tang Sanzang helped the abbot up and said, 'Old abbot, why such a grand gesture? Please speak slowly.'
13 It turned out that last year on this very night, while the abbot was reciting scriptures, he suddenly heard a cry after the wind passed. He hurried to search and found a woman outside the back gate. He asked, 'Who are you, and why are you crying here?' The woman replied, 'I am the princess of Tianzhu Kingdom. I was admiring flowers under the moon when the wind blew me here.'

[P9] 14 The abbot, unable to tell if the girl was real or not, and fearing trouble if a young woman stayed in the temple, had her walled up in an empty room, leaving only a small hole to pass food bowls. The monks gathered around, and the abbot said, 'She's a demon, caught and locked up by me.'
15 The girl, upon hearing this, immediately understood the abbot's intention. She pretended to be mad and foolish, babbling nonsense during the day, and only dared to secretly cry out for her parents at night when it was quiet. After a long time, the monks in the temple no longer paid any attention to her.

[P10] 16 The abbot had gone into town several times to inquire, but heard nothing. The king's deep palace was a forbidden place, and he could not go to ask. He could only send her coarse tea and plain food every day to keep her alive. In the blink of an eye, a year had passed.
17 The abbot continued, bowing several times: 'She is beautiful and dignified, like a princess. Regarding this matter, I earnestly hope, Reverend Master, that upon meeting the king, you can clarify the truth. If you can rescue this kind-hearted woman, not only will she be grateful for your kindness, but even I, this humble monk, will be relieved of this burden on my heart and will never forget your kindness.' The monk responded with great willingness.

[P11] 18 Tang Sanzang, burdened with worries, couldn't sleep. Before he knew it, the rooster crowed, and people at the temple gate called for the horses. Tang Sanzang woke his disciples, packed their belongings, and prepared to leave. At that moment, a monk came in and said, 'The abbot invites you masters to have some snacks.'
19 Pigsy, delighted at the prospect of food, ate a whole plate of buns, beamed with joy, and led the horse forward. Tang Sanzang thanked the monks, and the four disciples left the Bu Jin Temple, joining the caravan of merchants, chattering noisily as they set off down the road.

[P12] 20 The morning light was dim, on the 'Ji Ming Pass', the cold wind blew, and the rooster calls from near and far could be heard without ceasing.
21 At dawn, they passed the pass, had breakfast, and entered the royal city of Tianzhu. The merchants each sought lodging. Tang Sanzang and his disciples then checked into the 'Huitong Guesthouse' to stay.

[P13] 22 The驿丞 (head of the inn) learned about Tang Sanzang's background and destination, and treated him with even greater hospitality. When Tang Sanzang mentioned wanting to meet the king, the驿丞 said: 'Perfect! Today is the princess's lottery marriage day. The king is overjoyed; I guarantee you'll get your pass upon arrival.'
23 Upon hearing about the princess's marriage, Bajie said excitedly: 'Today I'll escort my master to court.' Sha Wujing replied: 'Brother Two, your face is too ugly; let Brother One go instead.' Tang Sanzang nodded in agreement. Bajie pouted and said: 'Hmph! Look at the three of us—none of us have good faces!'

[P14] 24 Tang Sanzang put on his robe, Wukong slung his satchel, and they stepped out of the inn gate. The streets were packed, bustling with people heading to the彩楼 to watch the princess throw the embroidered ball to choose a husband.
25 Wukong wanted to go along, but Tang Sanzang refused. Wukong said: 'Master, at the彩楼, we’re sure to see the princess. Isn’t this the perfect chance to verify her true identity?' Tang Sanzang nodded repeatedly and said: 'You’re right. I was momentarily distracted and forgot the matter entrusted to me by the abbot. Let’s go.'

[P15] 26 The master and his disciple were swept into the crowd, unable to control themselves, and pushed and crowded forward to the front of the彩楼.
27 Originally, this princess was a demon transformed. Knowing that Tang Sanzang was passing through Tianzhu Kingdom, it captured the real princess; then, pretending to hold a colorful ball marriage, it intended to sabotage Tang Sanzang's journey to obtain scriptures. At noon, the demon disguised itself as charming and beautiful, escorted by dozens of palace maids, and ascended the彩楼.

[P16] 28 The demoness spotted Tang Sanzang at once, took the embroidered ball and threw it, hitting Tang Sanzang squarely on the head. Tang Sanzang was greatly startled and thought to brush it away, but strangely, the ball rolled right into his sleeve.
29 From above, everyone shouted: 'We've hit a monk!' Chaos erupted below. The young noblemen who came to catch the ball, along with wealthy merchants hoping for luck, rushed forward, surrounded Tang Sanzang, and tried to snatch the ball.

[P17] 30 Wukong became furious, roared loudly, and with one bend of his waist grew over three zhang tall, frightening the group of young noblemen and wealthy sons, who screamed for their parents, stumbled and crawled, and all fled.
31 Wukong returned to his original form. The palace maidens and eunuchs came down from the楼 and bowed to Tang Sanzang, saying: "Noble sir, please enter the palace hall to celebrate the joyous occasion." Tang Sanzang hurriedly helped them up, then turned and scolded Wukong: "You mischievous monkey, you're at it again!"

[P18] 32 Wukong smiled: 'You agreed to come. The彩 ball hit you, what does it have to do with me?' Tang Sanzang, turning from anger to worry, said: 'What should I do?' After whispering for a while, Wukong said: 'This is called the 'Marriage to Subdue the Demon Plan'. Remember! I'm going back to the inn.'
33 Tang Sanzang was escorted by palace maidens to the front of the pavilion, and had no choice but to ride with the princess into the court to meet the king.

[P19] 34 The king, upon seeing that the groom was a monk, felt displeased. Tang Sanzang hurriedly explained his background, and finally pleaded: 'I beg Your Majesty to remember that I am a monk and cannot marry the princess. Spare my life, exchange my travel documents, and send me on my way to the West. I shall be eternally grateful!' 
35 The king intended to let Tang Sanzang go, but the princess refused to agree. The king immediately changed his expression and said to the princess: 'This is also a case of 'a thousand-mile姻缘 tied by a single thread'! Since you are happy, I shall issue an edict to announce it to the world, choose a favorable day, and let my daughter marry him.'

[P20] 36 Tang Sanzang did not thank the king, but kept shouting, “Let me go on my journey to fetch the scriptures!” The king frowned and said, “What an unreasonable monk! I offer you the wealth of an entire kingdom to become my son-in-law. Why don’t you know how to enjoy it? If you mention ‘fetching scriptures’ again, you’ll be executed!
37 Tang Sanzang trembled with fear, remembered Wukong’s clever plan, and hurriedly pleaded, “I thank Your Majesty! But may I give a few words of instruction to my three disciples and send them off to fetch the scriptures?” The king agreed and told his attendant, “Quickly go to the inn and bring the three young monks to see me.”

[P21] 38 After Wukong returned from the colorful pavilion and told Bajie and Sha Wujing about it, Bajie pounded his chest and stomped his feet, saying: 'This wonderful opportunity! Master refuses again. If only he had called me, how great it would be! If the embroidered ball had landed on my old pig's head, I wouldn't have to push and shove—I'd just run off to get married!' 
39 Sha Wujing pointed at Bajie's nose and scolded him harshly. Bajie wouldn't back down, and as the two were arguing, the postmaster arrived and reported: 'His Majesty commands: summon the three young masters to the palace immediately.'

[P22] 40 Pigsy said, 'Master has become a prince, come to invite us to the wedding feast!' Wukong, understanding the situation, frowned and said, 'Don't talk nonsense, hurry up and get ready, let's go to the court to see Master.'
41 Wukong and the other two entered the golden hall, standing tall without kneeling. Wukong saw his master standing by the side of the hall and angrily shouted, 'Your Majesty is unreasonable! My master is a noble person, how can he not even have a seat!'

[P23] 42 The king, seeing their ugly appearance, was greatly shocked and almost wanted to run away, but feared losing his dignity. He hurriedly ordered someone to bring a brocade stool and asked Tang Sanzang to sit down. Then, forcing himself to be brave, he asked: 'Three holy monks, quickly tell me your origins!'
43 As the three introduced themselves—one as 'Qitian Dasheng', one as 'Tianpeng Yuan Shuai', and one as 'Juanlian General'—the king, frightened, got off his dragon throne, approached Tang Sanzang, and respectfully said: 'Husband, my daughter has been matched with a living Buddha—how fortunate! How fortunate!'

[P24] 44 The king was delighted when suddenly the diviner reported: "Your Majesty, I have checked the almanac, and tomorrow is an auspicious day..." The king happily replied: "Quickly clean the imperial garden, and have the groom and his three disciples settle in. Arrange the dowry and banquet for the wedding tomorrow." 
45 The king dismissed court, and the officials dispersed. As soon as Tang Sanzang arrived at his residence in the imperial garden, he grabbed Wukong and said: "You rascal, you've caused me so much trouble! Tomorrow I'm supposed to get married—what am I going to do?"

[P25] 46 Wukong said: 'Master, don't worry. The other day at the彩楼, I couldn't see the princess's face, so I couldn't tell if she was real or fake. Tomorrow, at the wedding ceremony, I'll know at a glance. If she's a demon, I'll capture her; if she's the real princess, you can become a prince-in-law and enjoy prosperity here.'
47 Tang Sanzang became even more annoyed and scolded: 'If you keep talking nonsense, I'll chant the spell!' Wukong hurriedly said: 'Don't chant! Don't chant! I was just joking. If she's the real princess, when we crash the wedding ceremony, we'll surely be able to take you away!'

[P26] 48 Tang Sanzang finally felt at ease. Zhu Bajie said, 'Why give up being a prince consort to become a monk? Forget it, forget it. The vegetarian meal has been set for a long time. If you won't eat, I'm going to eat my fill and go to sleep.'
49 Meanwhile, the palace was busy preparing for the wedding, bustling with activity, the lights shining brightly as if it were daytime. The king, overjoyed, was about to go to the imperial garden to see the prince consort when suddenly an inner palace official reported, 'Your Majesty, the Empress has summoned you!'

[P27] 50 The king entered the palace, and the three queens came to pay their respects. The king pulled the princess aside and asked: 
"You threw the colorful ball to find a husband, and now you are matched with the holy monk. Are you satisfied?" The queen mother replied: "Quickly tell your father what's on your mind."
51 The princess knelt and said: "I heard that the groom has three disciples, who are extremely ugly. I am afraid to see them..." The king replied: "If you hadn't mentioned it, I almost forgot. They must not attend the wedding. Tomorrow morning, I will definitely send them out of the city."

[P28] 52 Early the next morning, the king sent an official to invite Tang Sanzang. Wukong thought: 'They must be sending us away so the master can marry...' He then told Tang Sanzang: 'If the king sends us away first, just agree. I'll come to protect you instantly. Don't be afraid.'
53 The master and disciples met the king. The king called Wukong forward and said: 'Here is an official document with the seal, for you. Also, thirty ingots of gold and silver as travel money. Go quickly to the West to fetch the scriptures, and there will be great rewards upon your return. The prince will remain here; you need not worry.'

[P29] 54 Wukong refused the silver and gold, took the pass document, and turned to leave. The panicked Tang Sanzang grabbed him, gritting his teeth and angrily said, 'You're all leaving without me?'
55 Wukong gripped Tang Sanzang's hand and gave him a glance, saying, 'Stay here as the prince consort. We'll get the scriptures and come back to see you.' The Tang Sanzang, half-believing and half-doubting, still wouldn't let go.

[P30] 56 The king hurriedly invited Master Tang to the palace and ordered officials to send Wukong and others to depart immediately. Master Tang had no choice but to let go. As the three walked down the golden hall, Bajie kept looking back and asked Wukong, "Are we really leaving?"
57 Wukong said nothing, led Bajie and Sha Wujing back to the inn, and told them, "You two stay here and don't move. If anyone asks anything, just say you don't know. I'll go protect our master."

[P31] 58 Good Great Sage, plucked a hair, blew on it and shouted: “Change!” Immediately, he transformed into a fake figure to stay at the inn, while his true body had already leapt into the air.
59 Wukong flipped again, transformed into a small bee, buzzed once, flew back to the golden palace, landed on Master Tang’s hat brim, and whispered: “Master, I’m here.”

[P32] 60 Tang Sanzang, upon hearing this, felt at ease. Shortly after, a palace official came to invite him to the wedding ceremony. The king was delighted and said to Tang Sanzang, 'Esteemed guest, the time has come. You should now go to the Yuanyang Palace for the wedding banquet.'
61 Tang Sanzang followed the king to the inner palace, where he saw lanterns hung and decorations strung, with music and drums filling the air. The palace maids and attendants were as beautiful as flowers and brocade. Tang Sanzang, however, had a worried look on his face and did not even glance at them.

[P33] 62 After a while, the queen and concubines escorted the princess out. Wukong looked and said, 'Master, the princess is fake. Let me use my magical form to seize her!' Tang Sanzang hurriedly said, 'No! No! Don't frighten the king.'
63 Wukong could not bear it any longer. He roared, revealed his true form, grabbed the princess, and scolded, 'You audacious beast! You've turned falsehood into truth, causing the king to be separated from his flesh and blood, and you still dare to deceive my master. Today is your last day!'

[P34] 64 In the Jiuque Palace, everyone cried and screamed in chaos. Tang Sanzang panicked and trembled as he hugged the king, saying, 'Don't be afraid, don't be afraid, this is my mischievous disciple using his magic power.'
65 The demon, seeing she could no longer deceive them, broke free, dropped her clothes, ran to the land temple in the imperial garden, pulled out a short stick shaped like a pestle, and turned to wildly attack Wukong. Wukong met her with his staff, and they fought fiercely, neither able to gain the upper hand.

[P35] 66 Fighting and fighting, they displayed their supernatural powers, flying through the clouds and fighting in mid-air. The sight terrified the court officials and frightened the entire city's people; the king covered his eyes and trembled. Tang Sanzang said, 'Your Majesty, don't be afraid. Your princess is a demon. Once we capture it, you'll see for yourself.'
67 Some bold concubines brought the princess's clothes and jewelry to the queen and said, 'These are what the princess wore. Now she is fighting naked with that monk—she must be a demon!' At this, the king and the concubines calmed down a bit and dared to take a look.

[P36] 68 The two fought for a long time, neither gaining the upper hand. Wukong tossed his staff into the air and shouted: 
"Change!" Instantly, one became ten, ten became a hundred, a hundred became a thousand... In mid-air, it looked like snakes and dragons rolling and tumbling, wildly attacking the demon.
69 The demon panicked and fled, turning into a gust of wind. Wukong retrieved his staff and chased after it. As they neared the Western Heaven Gate, Wukong shouted: "Guardians of the Heavenly Gate, quickly block the demon—don't let it escape!"

[P37] 70 The demon turned and fled straight south, with Wukong in hot pursuit. Suddenly reaching a big mountain, in the blink of an eye, the demon vanished.
71 Wukong could not find the demon, and fearing it might sneak back to the palace to harm his master, he memorized the mountain's appearance, did a somersault, and returned to Tianzhu Kingdom.

[P38] 72 Wukong descended into the palace, told his master what had happened. The king, upon hearing this, grabbed Tang Sanzang and asked, 'If the princess is a demon, where is my real princess?' Wukong replied, 'Wait for me to capture the fake one, and the real one will naturally return.'
73 At this moment, the king and concubines were no longer afraid. They approached Wukong and bowed, saying, 'Please, holy monk, quickly rescue the princess and bring her back to the palace!' Wukong said, 'Your Majesty and my master should go to the throne hall, the ladies should return to the palace, and summon my younger brother to protect my master. Then I can go and subdue the demon.'

[P39] 74 The king said repeatedly, 'As you command!' Wukong, seeing Bajie and Sha僧 arrive, gave them instructions, then took off into the sky with a somersault. The court officials looked up and bowed one by one.
75 Wukong returned to that mountain to search, but still saw no trace. He summoned the local spirit and asked, 'What is the name of this mountain? How many demons are there? Speak quickly, and I will spare your sins!' The spirit replied, 'This mountain is called Maoying Mountain. There are only a few rabbit holes in the mountain; it has never hidden demons.'

[P40] 76 Wukong told the Land God about his recent pursuit of the demon. The Land God was greatly surprised and hurriedly said:
"Ah! I didn't know that... I'll quickly lead the Great Sage to find it!
77 The Land God led Wukong in searching all over the mountain, startling wild rabbits that scattered in all directions. Upon reaching the summit, they found a large cave blocked with stones. The Land God said: 'It seems there's a demon here, Great Sage, go in and capture it.'

[P41] 78 Wukong smashed the rocks with his staff. The demon suddenly charged out, fighting and fleeing at the same time, and angrily grabbed the Land God, shouting: 'Who told you to bring him here? You old fool, I'll get you back later!'
79 The demon ran ahead, and Wukong chased behind. As the demon seemed to be unable to hold on, Wukong raised his staff to strike, when suddenly a voice called from the sky: 'Great Sage, don't strike! Spare him!'

[P42] 80 The one shouting was the Taiyin Xingjun and the Chang'e Fairy. After hearing them, Wukong learned that the demon was the Jade Rabbit from the Moon Palace, who had secretly opened the golden lock and left to cause trouble. Wukong thought to himself: 'No wonder I didn't recognize its weapon—it's the pestle used for grinding medicine!'
81 Wukong thought again: it had impersonated the princess and deceived his master, so he couldn't help but swing his staff. Fortunately, the star lord blocked him; the demon dodged quickly, and the staff didn't hit its vital spot, so it wasn't killed.

[P43] 82 The Star Lord pleaded repeatedly. Wukong said, “I can spare you, but you must make it reveal its true form and bring it to Tianzhu Kingdom for the king to see.” The Star Lord nodded in agreement. Turning back, he pointed with his hand, and the demon rolled on the ground, instantly transforming into a jade rabbit.
83 The stars and moon were bright. The king and Tang Sanzang were waiting for Wukong to return with the demon, when suddenly they heard a voice from the sky: “King, Queen, concubines, and officials, come and see! These two are the Star Lord of the Moon and the Fairy Chang’e. This jade rabbit is your false princess…”

[P44] 84 The king and others looked on, each bowing to the sky. A flash of golden light appeared, and Wukong descended before the palace. The Star Lord, Chang'e, and the Jade Rabbit were already gone.
85 The king invited Wukong to the hall and asked, 'Thank you, holy monk, for capturing the false princess. But where is the real princess?' Wukong smiled and replied, 'If the false one doesn't leave, the true one won't come. It's already late at night. I'll return the real princess to you by tomorrow morning.'

[P45] 86 Nothing happened that night. At dawn, the king summoned Tang Sanzang and his disciples to inquire about the princess. Tang Sanzang recounted everything he had seen and heard at 'Bu Jin Temple'. The king burst into tears and immediately issued an order to personally go to 'Bu Jin Temple' to fetch the princess.
87 The king invited Tang Sanzang and his disciples to accompany him. Wukong twisted his waist and arrived at the temple early. After telling the abbot, he startled all the monks in the temple, who quickly put on their robes, set up incense tables, and prepared to welcome the king.

[P46] 88 Wukong waited in the temple for a long time before the king arrived. The king could hardly wait to see the princess and ordered the abbot to lead the way. As soon as the princess saw people coming, she started acting crazy again. The abbot knelt and reported: 'This madwoman is the princess who was blown here by the wind last year.'
89 The king ordered the door to be opened quickly. The queen recognized her daughter's face, ignored the dirt, and cried out in grief, embracing her. The deep bond of blood moved everyone present to tears.

[P47] 90 The princess bathes and changes clothes. The king orders the princess to first thank the Tang Monk and his disciples for saving her life, and then thank the abbot for his hospitality. He bestows the title 'Bao Guo Seng Guan' upon the abbot, issues an edict to rebuild the temple, and after the monks have expressed their gratitude, the king returns to the palace.
91 After returning to the kingdom, the Tang Monk bids farewell to depart westward. The king, unable to keep him, holds a farewell banquet, orders a portrait to be made and enshrined, and presents rich gifts as thanks. The Tang Monk politely declines. Wukong says, "As long as the king agrees to one thing, it would be better than a portrait or rich gifts." The king hurriedly replies, "Please tell me what it is!"

[P48] 92 Wukong said: 'Before the 'Bujin Temple' there is a 'Baijiao Mountain'. In the mountain, centipedes block the path and harm people. Your Majesty, you could select a thousand strong roosters and release them into the mountain to eliminate this menace, making travel easier for merchants and travelers. Wouldn't that be a great good deed?
93 The king was delighted and immediately selected a thousand red-crowned roosters, sending them to the 'Baijiao Mountain'. Strange as it may seem, the centipede spirits, several zhang long, upon seeing the flock of roosters, became straight sticks and were eaten at will. In just one day, all the centipedes, big and small, in the 'Baijiao Mountain' were eaten by the roosters.

[P49] 94 The 'Baijiao Mountain' was renamed 'Baohua Mountain', and from then on, it was open for travel day and night. The portraits of Tang Monk and his disciples were placed in the 'Shenseng Pavilion' at the summit, where the king, ministers, and people of Tianzhu Kingdom would forever remember these four monks who journeyed to obtain scriptures. To learn what happens next, please read the final volume, 'Pilgrimage to Ling Mountain'.

[P1] 本页为《西游记》连环画《天竺国》的封面，展示了原著、改编者、绘画者及出版社信息，并配有相关插图。
[P2] 本页为《西游记》连环画《天竺国》的内容提要，介绍了画册改编自原著第九十三至九十五回，讲述唐僧师徒在天竺国和蜈蚣岭除妖的故事，并附有第一幅插图及文字，描述师徒四人行至布金禅寺的情景。
[P3] 唐僧师徒行至布金禅寺，唐僧联想到佛经中给孤独长者用金砖布地的典故，八戒戏言想抢金砖送人，悟空呵斥后众人笑着进入山门。
[P4] 唐僧师徒四人来到布金禅寺山门，客商们见他们后纷纷让路；随后他们进入寺内，遇见一位老和尚，老和尚认出他们是大唐神僧，便邀请他们入室用茶。
[P5] 唐僧师徒在布金禅寺内，唐僧询问寺庙由来，老和尚讲述典故，八戒听后四处寻找金砖，引得悟空和沙僧暗笑；随后唐僧询问山门下为何有众多客商，众和尚解释因百脚山下鸡鸣关有蜈蚣精拦路，商旅需在庙中借宿，待五更鸡叫后才敢过关。
[P6] 唐僧师徒在布金禅寺安顿后，决定鸡叫时动身；夜晚，唐僧与悟空在廊下散步，小和尚通报院主到来，老和尚前来迎接，唐僧连忙回礼。
[P7] 院主邀请唐僧师徒前往‘给孤独长者’请佛讲经的旧址参观，众人在途中歇息时，夜深人静，忽然听到一个女孩的啼哭声。
[P8] 唐僧听到哭声后心酸落泪，院主跪拜相迎；院主回忆去年今夜在寺中发现一位自称天竺国公主的女子，称其被风刮至寺中。
[P9] 院主因怀疑女子身份，将其囚禁于空房，仅留小洞送饭，并称其为妖邪；女子为求自保，装疯卖傻，夜深时偷偷哭泣，久而久之被和尚们忽视。
[P10] 院主讲述囚禁女子一年的经过，并请求唐僧帮忙辨明其身份、救拔善良；唐僧慨然答应。画面显示女子被囚于房中，以及院主向唐僧等人诉说时的场景。
[P11] 唐僧师徒在布金禅寺过夜后，天亮时准备启程，院主派人送来点心，八戒吃完后牵马先行，师徒四人与商队一同踏上旅途。
[P12] 唐僧师徒在黎明时分通过鸡鸣关，进入天竺国皇城后，投宿于会同馆驿。
[P13] 唐僧师徒抵达天竺国后，驿丞告知今日是公主抛彩招婿之期，可助唐僧见国王。八戒听后跃跃欲试，想保师父上朝，沙僧劝他让悟空去，八戒不服，抱怨三人皆相貌不佳。
[P14] 唐僧师徒离开馆驿，前往彩楼观看公主抛绣球招驸马，悟空提议借此机会辨明公主真假，唐僧随即同意前往。
[P15] 唐僧师徒被人群推挤至彩楼前，画面揭示公主实为妖精所变，其目的为破坏唐僧取经，真公主已被摄走，妖精正由宫女簇拥登上彩楼。
[P16] 妖精将绣球抛向唐僧，绣球落在他头上并滚入袖中；楼上人群欢呼，楼下众人围住唐僧抢夺彩球，场面混乱。
[P17] 孙悟空因不满绣球被抛向唐僧而大怒，变身高大吓跑众人；随后恢复原形，宫娥太监前来请唐僧入朝堂，唐僧埋怨悟空又捉弄自己。
[P18] 悟空向唐僧解释‘依婚降妖计’，并离开；唐僧被宫娥簇拥，与假公主一同乘辇前往朝堂见国王。
[P19] 唐僧被带入朝堂，国王见其为和尚心生不悦，唐僧恳求放行；国王本想放人，但假公主坚持要成婚，国王遂答应择日完婚。
[P20] 唐僧在朝堂上拒绝接受驸马之位，坚持要取经，惹怒国王被下令斩首；他随即想起悟空的计策，请求传唤徒弟们，国王准奏并命人去馆驿传唤三徒。
[P21] 悟空回到馆驿后向八戒和沙僧讲述彩楼抛绣球之事，八戒懊恼自己未能被选中，沙僧则斥责他，两人正争吵时，驿丞前来传旨，要三位徒弟上殿见国王。
[P22] 八戒误以为师父成了驸马，高兴地想吃喜酒，悟空提醒他去朝见师父；三人上殿后，悟空见师父在殿旁侍立无座，怒斥国王不讲道理。
[P23] 唐僧的三位徒弟孙悟空、猪八戒、沙僧被召上朝，国王见他们相貌丑陋惊慌失措，但得知他们身份后，因唐僧是‘活佛’而欣喜若狂，恭敬地称唐僧为驸马。
[P24] 国王选定明日为婚期，命人准备婚礼；唐僧回到住处后向孙悟空抱怨，担心明日成婚的困境。
[P25] 孙悟空向唐僧保证，明日拜堂时定能分辨真假公主，并开玩笑说若为真公主可大闹皇宫带师父离开，唐僧听后生气要念紧箍咒，悟空连忙解释是玩笑话。
[P26] 唐僧因孙悟空的保证而放心，八戒则抱怨不娶公主而要当和尚，想吃素斋后睡觉。与此同时，宫中正忙于筹备婚礼，国王准备去御花园看驸马时，被内宫官告知正宫娘娘有请。
[P27] 国王进宫后，三宫皇后朝拜，国王询问公主对与唐僧成婚是否满意。公主跪下表示害怕见到唐僧的三个徒弟，国王随即决定不让徒弟们参加婚礼，并计划次日将他们送出城外。
[P28] 第二天一早，国王派人请唐僧，孙悟空猜是想打发他们离开以便成婚，便安慰师父。师徒见国王后，国王赐予通关文牒和盘缠，让他们速去西天取经，并称会留下驸马，不必挂念。
[P29] 孙悟空拒绝国王赏赐的金银，拿过通关文牒后准备离开，唐僧急忙拉住他，担心被留下；孙悟空安慰唐僧，承诺取经归来后会回来看他，唐僧仍不放心，不肯放手。
[P30] 国王请唐僧上殿并命人送孙悟空等人立即启程，唐僧无奈放手。八戒回头张望，询问是否真要离开。孙悟空带八戒和沙僧先回馆驿，嘱咐他们不要乱动，自己去保护师父。
[P31] 孙悟空拔毫毛变出假身留在馆驿，真身飞回金殿，化作小蜜蜂落在唐僧帽沿上，悄悄报信。
[P32] 国王邀请唐僧参加婚礼，唐僧随国王前往后宫，见宫中张灯结彩、鼓乐喧天，但唐僧愁眉不展，对眼前景象视而不见。
[P33] 孙悟空发现公主是妖怪所变，欲出手制服，唐僧劝阻；孙悟空怒不可遏，现出原形，揪住假公主痛骂，揭露其欺骗国王、离间骨肉的罪行。
[P34] 在鸠鹊宫中，众人因孙悟空揭露妖怪而惊慌失措，唐僧抱住国王安抚。妖怪挣脱后逃至御花园土地庙，取出短棍与孙悟空激烈交战，双方打得难解难分。
[P35] 孙悟空与妖怪在空中激烈交战，唐僧安抚国王；妃子们拿出公主的衣物证明其为妖怪，国王和后妃这才敢看。
[P36] 孙悟空与妖怪在空中激战，不分胜负；孙悟空变出无数分身围攻妖怪，妖怪慌忙化作清风逃走，孙悟空紧追至西天门，呼喊天门守卫拦住妖怪。
[P37] 孙悟空追击妖怪至一座大山，妖怪突然消失；孙悟空因担心妖怪潜回皇宫加害师父，便记下山形，一个筋斗返回天竺国。
[P38] 孙悟空向国王说明公主是妖怪所变，国王焦急询问真公主下落，孙悟空承诺抓住假公主后真公主自会回来。随后国王和后妃向孙悟空求救，孙悟空安排国王和唐僧上殿、妃子回宫，并让师弟保护师父，自己前去降妖。
[P39] 孙悟空安排八戒和沙僧保护师父后腾空而去，满朝文武望空叩拜；随后他返回妖怪消失的山中寻找，向土地神询问山名和妖邪情况，得知此山名为毛颖山，向来无妖。
[P40] 孙悟空向土地神讲述追妖经过，土地神引他满山寻找，在山顶发现一个被石块堵住的洞穴，认为其中有妖邪，建议孙悟空进去捉拿。
[P41] 孙悟空捣碎石块后，妖怪冲出并责骂土地神；随后孙悟空追击妖怪，妖怪不支，空中有人喊话让孙悟空手下留情。
[P42] 孙悟空得知妖怪是广寒宫的玉兔后，愤怒地欲将其打死，但被太阴星君和嫦娥仙子拦下，妖怪因闪躲及时未被击中要害。
[P43] 孙悟空在太阴星君和嫦娥仙子的求情下，同意饶恕妖怪，但要求其现出原形。妖怪变回玉兔后，星君等人将其带回天竺国，向国王等人揭示其为假公主的真相。
[P44] 孙悟空降落在宫殿前，太阴星君、嫦娥和玉兔已不见踪影；国王询问真公主下落，孙悟空表示天明便会还回真公主。
[P45] 天亮后，国王请唐僧师徒讲述公主之事，得知真相后悲痛万分，决定亲自前往布金寺接回公主；悟空提前到达寺庙，通知院主后，全寺和尚准备迎接国王。
[P46] 国王在孙悟空的陪同下抵达布金寺，院主引路见到装疯的真公主；皇后认出女儿后不顾污秽抱头痛哭，场面感人至深，众人无不落泪。
[P47] 公主沐浴更衣后，国王命其感谢唐僧师徒和院主，并封院主为‘报国僧官’，重修寺院后回朝。唐僧辞行，国王设宴饯行并赠厚礼，唐僧婉拒，孙悟空提出一个请求，国王答应。
[P48] 孙悟空向国王建议用千只雄鸡消灭布金寺前百脚山的蜈蚣精，国王采纳建议，公鸡果然在一天内将所有蜈蚣吃光。
[P49] 本页描述了百脚山改名为宝华山，唐僧师徒画像被供奉于山顶神僧阁，天竺国百姓永远纪念他们。同时，页面下方列出了《西游记》连环画的完整目录，共35册，最后一册为《灵山参佛祖》。
[P50] 本页为《西游记》连环画《天竺国》的版权页，列出了原著作者、改编者、绘者、出版社、印刷信息、ISBN及定价等出版信息。
